name: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd
title: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd - 540716 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Motor loss ratio held near 65.4% H1 and management says no further Shishupal reserving, but Q2 combined ratio rose to 104.5% and H1 PAT fell 5.8%, so the capital-cycle signal is mixed and supply-side evidence is thin.

summary.headline: ICICI Lombard Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27.5% YoY to ₹10.31 bn, while H1 PAT fell 5.8% to ₹14.54 bn on a weaker Q1 and Motor TP reserving.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 profitability improved sharply: PBT grew 27.8% to ₹13.59 bn and PAT 27.5% to ₹10.31 bn, with combined ratio at 104.5% (102.7% ex-CAT). H1 was weaker, with PAT down 5.8% to ₹14.54 bn and combined ratio at 105.2%, reflecting the Q1 Supreme Court (Shishupal) Motor TP reserving of ₹1.65 bn and Q1 commercial large losses. GDPI grew 5.4% in H1 versus industry 8.9%, though ex-Crop and Mass Health Q2 growth of 13.9% was ahead of industry 13.2%. Management said no further Motor TP reserve top-up is needed and that the judgment is now business as usual.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: H1 growth 13.0% vs industry 13.1%, market share 10.3%; mix PC 49.8%, 2W 28.1%, CV 22.1%. Motor combined ratio 108.3% in Q1 FY27 vs industry 131.4%; management cites ~23 pts gap. H1 Motor loss ratio ~65.4% vs 66.6% last year.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: H1 growth 26.8% vs industry 21.0%. Retail Health grew 66.4% (industry 32.0%), share 4.7% in H1 and 5.0% exiting September. Group Health grew 15.4%, share stable at 8.8%; Group Health loss ratio 97.9% in Q2 vs 93.7% a year ago.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Ex-Fire growth 20.0% in Q2 and 13.2% in H1. Fire de-growth moderated to 21.2% in Q2 from 32.1% in Q1, with September at -6.0%. Fire market share 11.9% in Q2 (11.4% prior year); Marine cargo 19.0%; Engineering 16.4%; Liability 16.6%.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Management said it was deliberately cautious in underwriting Crop this year, which muted headline top-line growth against NEP growth.

guidance_outlook: Management expects earned premium momentum to continue into Q3 and Q4, with gross premium growth ahead of industry.
No further Motor TP reserving requirement anticipated after the ₹1.65 bn Q1 provision; judgment treated as business as usual, with ongoing monitoring.
Motor loss ratio range kept at 65% to 67% (aggregate Motor), with Group Health underwritten around mid-90s and Retail Health at 65% to 70%.
Digital sourcing to be scaled from 6.0% to 15% of business under a defined roadmap.
Expense of management kept within the 30% limit on an annual basis; the draft 25% limit is seen as a positive for the company.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Digital journeys handled 73% of customer interactions vs 39% a year ago; IL TakeCare app has 23.3 mn downloads.
Health underwriting WhatsApp GenAI bot used in over 40% of agency new business daily.
demand_pricing: Industry vehicle sales grew 21.1% in H1 FY27 and 26.9% in Q2, with September up 32.0%; management expects Motor growth to moderate on a higher base from Q3 after GST reform effects.
Retention improved 3% to 5% across retail lines (Motor and Health) in H1 vs last year.
Banca and corporate tie-ups contribute 12.5% to 15% of full-year premium, with single-digit exposure outside ICICI.
Reinsurance accepted is kept at a single-digit share of the overall book; management says no change in book quality in Q2.
Q2 Motor OD loss ratio was hit by Q2 flood events: ~₹118 mn of flood losses vs ~₹74-75 mn last year.

qa_highlights.question: Did Q1 Motor TP loss ratio jump reflect the Supreme Court judgment, and is more provisioning needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹1.65 bn was reserved in Q1 and no further reserving is needed; the judgment is now business as usual and development will be monitored over long cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Will IRDAI distribution reforms and commission cuts pressure third-party tariffs and renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reform is a recalibration that may lower costs and aid penetration, and tariff impact is uncertain. Retention rose 3% to 5%, and the company is increasing its renewal focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Group Health and Retail Health loss ratio trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Group Health loss ratio was 97.9% in Q2 vs 93.7% a year ago, but down from ~99.9% in Q1. Retail indemnity was 64.6% vs 65.4% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Motor OD loss ratio deteriorate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to Q2 flood events (~₹118 mn vs ~₹74-75 mn last year). Ex-CAT, OD loss ratio was sequentially better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did commission and other opex ratios rise in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a higher retail mix, which carries higher acquisition cost but better loss outcomes, and said opex changes are business as usual.

qa_highlights.question: How would the 25% expense-of-management limit affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is well within the 30% EOM limit on an annual basis and sees the draft 25% limit as a positive for market share.

risks_watch: Motor TP tail development after the Shishupal judgment; any reserve release or strengthening in later quarters.
Distribution reform outcome: commission cuts, possible TP tariff changes, and POSP disruption in CV TP.
Commercial lines loss experience: Q1 large losses and Fire de-growth continuing; September Fire at -6.0%.
Base effect from GST reforms in Q3 and Q4 may moderate Motor growth.
IFRS transition impact not yet quantified; management said a separate briefing will follow.
Crop underwriting caution and Q2 flood/CAT events may weigh on loss ratios.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Motor momentum, Health and Q2 recovery, but guarded on Commercial line loss trajectory and on the timing and economics of the distribution reforms, which management called "early days". Management was evasive on IFRS impact, saying it would revert at a later date.
key_quotes: Honestly, it is now a part of our business as usual and genuinely, we do not believe the need for us to separately call out any specific additional charge consequent to the Supreme Court judgment.
Motor is not a discretionary purchase. Motor is the law of the land where you are expected, if you are plying your vehicles on road, you are expected to have a coverage.
And the range that we have always spoken is to kind of see the book running at between 65% to 67%.
